name: Sail a small dinghy
time: A week-long course, then a season
blurb: Wind awareness, points of sail, tacking and gybing. Once it clicks, sailing stops feeling like magic and starts feeling like a set of rules you can apply.
gear: A beginner course — this is one to learn from an instructor
steps: Learn to feel where the wind is coming from, constantly. Everything else in sailing depends on that one awareness.
Learn the points of sail: close hauled, reaching, running, and the no-go zone into the wind.
Learn sail trim: let it out until it luffs, then pull in until it stops. That rule alone covers most situations.
Learn to tack — turning the bow through the wind — with the sequence of words, tiller and body movement in order.
Learn to gybe, which is the one that catches people out: control the boom, keep your head down.
Learn capsize recovery deliberately, in warm sheltered water with support. It removes the fear.
tips: Sit facing the sail with the tiller behind you. Steering feels backwards until it does not.
Do a proper course. Sailing has genuine hazards and self-teaching from videos is a poor substitute.
proof: You sail a triangular course unaided, tacking and gybing under control, and recover from a capsize.
